Package com.csse3200.game.areas.terrain.map

Record Class BackdropLayer

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.csse3200.game.areas.terrain.map.BackdropLayer
Record Components:
texture - the image; one that fills the view must tile seamlessly in every direction it moves
scroll - for a layer filling the view, how far the artwork moves relative to the camera: 0 is fixed to the screen, 1 moves with the tiles
driftX - for a layer filling the view, constant sideways movement in world units per second
driftY - for a layer filling the view, constant upward movement in world units per second
spansMap - true to span the map rather than fill the view
rows - the band of the map the layer is seen in, or null to be seen everywhere
alpha - how opaque the layer is drawn, from 0 (unseen) to 1 (solid)
flicker - for a layer that is a strip of frames shown now and then, such as distant lightning, how it plays; null for an ordinary layer
public record BackdropLayer(String texture, float scroll, float driftX, float driftY, boolean spansMap, BackdropLayer.Rows rows, float alpha, BackdropLayer.Flicker flicker) extends Record
One image of a parallax backdrop or overlay, drawn behind or in front of the tile layers.

A backdrop is a stack of these, listed back to front. A layer is drawn one of two ways:

  • Filling the view, pinned to the screen, sliding its artwork sideways as the camera pans so distant layers appear to move less than near ones. This suits a level explored sideways.
  • Spanning the map: as wide as the map and as tall as its own proportions make it, rising more slowly than the camera so its bottom meets the map's bottom and its top the map's top. The shorter the image, the further away it seems. This suits a level that is climbed.
